newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa exchange draws up plan for $/rand futures.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa exchange draws up plan for $/rand futures.

text.p: The South African Futures Exchange (Safex) has drawn up specifications for a dollar/rand futures contract which could trade once exchange controls were eased sufficiently, chief executive Stuart Rees said on Wednesday.
Rees added, however, that it was not possible to say when that might be.
"These plans were drawn up at a point in time when it looked as though the relaxation of exchange controls was likelier than it does today," he told Reuters.

The sharp fall in the rand this year has delayed any major easing in controls, according to analysts, although the government remains committed to the eventual removal of exchange controls on residents.
The contract would have the same delivery dates as Safex's existing equity futures -- March, June, September, December -- and would be for around $100,000.
It could play a valuable role in the rand foreign exchange forward market where the central Reserve Bank has a long-term goal of reducing its presence.
